n: This psalm is an acrostic: after ‘Hallelujah,’ each half-line begins with the next letter of the Hebrew alphabet. The psalmist praises God wholeheartedly, both among close friends and in the larger congregation.
God’s works are great, and those who delight in them study them closely. Faith includes curiosity about God’s ways.
All God does is full of splendor and majesty, and his righteousness never ends.
God made his wonders memorable — through festivals like Passover — so his people would never forget his grace and compassion.
He gave food — like manna in the wilderness — to those who reverence him, and never forgets his covenant.
He showed his power by giving Israel the lands of other nations.
Everything God does is faithful and just; all his commandments can be trusted.
His commands stand firm forever, grounded in truth and uprightness.
God sent redemption to his people — as at the Exodus, and ultimately through Jesus Christ — and made his covenant permanent. ‘Reverend’ means awe-inspiring.

f.g: Worthy of reverence; awesome. In scripture used only of God.

n: The famous conclusion: reverence for the Lord is where wisdom begins. Real understanding comes from living his commandments, not just knowing them.

f.w: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom
